Write exactly one scene of plain English prose within the scene_contract word budget.
Use the frozen story intent, StoryState, route, relevant_character_canon and prop_authorization_policy. Do not advance to the next scene.
Relevant character canon is immutable identity truth. Never change a named character's age, identity terms or pronouns.
Prop authorization is fail-closed: do not materialize any new portable or action-capable physical prop unless it is already authorized by StoryState, SceneContract, immutable canon, or authorized_actionable_props. Do not introduce rope, cord, tools, weapons, containers, ladders, boats, lights, hooks or reusable equipment as scenery. Fixed structural features explicitly required by the contract are allowed.
Every required_event is a structured specification: dramatize ALL its predicates with exactly the specified actors, actions, targets and required observer.
Use only allowed provenance; never invent forbidden clues, world rules or lore.
DIRECT_OBSERVATION means an event visible in the scene, not a separate physical clue.
If separate_physical_clue_required is false, no additional clue is needed or requested.
An observer's ACKNOWLEDGE may be seeing and accepting the indicated observation, including a reluctant response; no separate declaration of proof is necessary.
Do not add persistent facts or violate entry/exit state, canon or forbidden actions.
If rewrite is supplied, repair all blocking findings while preserving the same contract.
Output prose only, without headings, evidence lists, JSON or commentary.

The spatial_contract is authoritative and shared with the guard. Use only its declared edges, passage directions and entity permissions. In particular a doorway's endpoint cannot turn into a different entry room or interior ascent.
Its entry access_constraints persist from previous scenes. An active blocker remains active until the explicit RELEASE operation visibly occurs. A release is a change in bodily position that opens the named approach; it does not imply affection, permission or trust. Show the release before ACCESS. Never silently bypass a blocking body.
Render every spatial operation as a visible action in the listed chronological order. Use distinct, non-overlapping short clauses for successive operations, including individual members of a group; each clause must establish its subject, action and endpoint. LOCATE means establish an entity's visible position for the first time, not invent its arrival. MOVE traverses the specified edge. A carried entity can MOVE with its carrier along the same declared passage. Do not invent detours or extra actions to satisfy bookkeeping.

replaced by a reward.","status":"OPEN","target_scene_id":"SC06"}]},"artifact":{"schema_name":"spineforge-relay.scene-artifact.v1","scene_id":"SC03","attempt":1,"status":"ACCEPTED","prose":"Daylight filled the dry upper room. Across it, Ekin saw the sea dragon crouched beside the lighthouse nest, her broad body shining with seawater.

A small shape stirred within the nest. The dragon hatchling was there, no bigger than a cat. Its wings fluttered, but it stayed firmly on its feet, bright-eyed and unhurt.

The mother dragon shifted sideways. She planted herself across the approach to the nest, blocking Ekin’s path.

Then she lowered her head and placed the brass compass in the nest beside the hatchling.

Ekin’s breath caught. She saw the compass clearly, close enough for daylight to flash across its worn brass. She took one quick step forward, but Duru caught her attention with a sharp whisper.

“Wait. Look at the little one.”

Duru had noticed the hatchling. Ekin looked again and saw it watching the compass, then pressing close to its mother’s side.

“That doesn’t make the compass hers,” Ekin said.

“No,” Duru replied. “But the mother is guarding the way.”

Ekin searched the room for another approach. Beside the wall, both girls saw a narrow turning stair leading downward toward the lower maintenance room. Far below, visible through the stair opening, daylight and gray sea showed beyond a fixed iron grate.

Duru glanced from the stair back to the dragon. “Don’t rush her. We need to think.”

“My grandfather’s compass is right there.”

“And so is the dragon.”

Ekin kept her eyes on the brass circle in the nest. The mother remained across the approach, silent and unmoving. Impatience tightened Ekin’s hands inside her jacket sleeves.

“You can think,” she muttered. “I’m not leaving without
